stories.title: Fortune Lands Record $817M From Tyko Capital to Build Miami Faena Condo Towers
stories.excerpt: Adi Chugh’s Tyko Capital doled out Florida’s largest-ever construction loan: $817 million for the Faena-branded, waterfront condo development in Miami, the project’s sponsors announced Wednesday. Fortune International Group and Kar Properties are developing the two-tower project at 24 Southwest Fourth Street, facing the Miami River, across from Brickell City Centre. Both skyscrapers will rise 68 stories, housing 217 units each. Construction is expected to be completed in 2030. The 1.8-acre, Rafael Viñoly Architects-designed project has generated more than $500 million in sales to date, including the $30 million purchase of a penthouse, according to the sponsors. The debt transaction “demonstrates the depth of confidence in the project and the continued global appetite for best-in-class real estate in Miami,” Edgardo Defortuna, president and CEO of Fortune International Group, said in a statement. Despite interest rate hikes, lenders are still funneling mammoth construction loans for luxury condo projects in South Florida, typically after strong presales. Earlier this week, Fortune International Group, alongside Château Group, secured a $463 million loan to finish one condo tower at the St. Regis Residences condo development in Sunny Isles Beach. In 2022, Defortuna bought the Downtown Miami site for $58.8 million, partnering with KAR Properties, which had owned it since 2013, according to property records. In 2015, New York-based KAR Properties had launched sales for a luxury condo project, but construction never started. The land, which is surrounded by three condo buildings inside a gated community, stayed vacant. In 2023, Bank OZK supplied a $38 million loan for marketing costs and site work for the Faena Residences, which marks the first condo development for the hotel brand, founded by Alan Faena and billionaire Len Blavatnik in 2000. It operates an oceanfront hotel and nearby cultural event spaces in Miami Beach as well as hotels in New York and Buenos Aires. T
bullets: Tyko Capital closes $817M construction loan, Florida's largest ever, for Faena Miami condo towers.
Fortune/KAR developing 434-unit, 68-story twin towers at Miami River; $500M+ presales; completion 2030.
Deep-pocket lender confidence persists despite rate hikes; signals strong institutional appetite for luxury Miami waterfront.
stories.summary: Tyko Capital funded an $817 million construction loan for Fortune International Group and KAR Properties' dual 68-story Faena-branded condo towers in Miami's Brickell submarket (24 SW 4th Street), totaling 434 units. The project has generated over $500 million in presales, including a $30 million penthouse deal. Completion is targeted for 2030. The large, institutional-grade debt commitment signals sustained lender confidence in Miami luxury residential despite elevated interest rates.
stories.impact: This signals strong capital availability for trophy multifamily/condo in Miami's Brickell/Miami River submarkets, even as rate environment remains elevated. The presale velocity and institutional debt appetite suggest pent-up demand from foreign and high-net-worth buyers remains robust, which can anchor rental demand in surrounding submarkets as buyers hold units or lease short-term. Developers with land positions in competing Brickell/riverfront corridors should expect intensified competition for capital and accelerated timelines.

stories.title: Sagard, La Caisse Acquire East Bay Industrial Outdoor Storage
stories.excerpt: Sagard Real Estate (SRE) on Wednesday announced the acquisition of 6691 Clark Ave., a fully leased industrial outdoor storage (IOS) property in Newark, within the infill East Bay submarket. Seller and pricing were not disclosed. The acquisition marks the second Bay Area IOS investment and further expands the IOS joint venture between SRE and global investment group La Caisse. The fully secured, paved, and lit 2.84-acre site includes an approximately 22,100-square-foot industrial building with 22-foot clear heights, making it suitable for contractor yard/materials storage, equipment rental and sales, light distribution, and other mission-critical IOS uses. “Newark’s access to the East Bay’s transportation network is central to the appeal of this investment,” said Tom Stover, managing director, acquisitions at SRE. “The property combines that connectivity with a secured, functional site in a supply-constrained infill market. As we pursue additional IOS acquisitions in the Bay Area, our focus remains on established infill locations with outdoor space and access to regional transportation infrastructure that support the day-to-day operations of industrial users.” . The post Sagard, La Caisse Acquire East Bay Industrial Outdoor Storage appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sagard Real Estate/La Caisse acquire 2.84-acre industrial outdoor storage site in Newark, East Bay, fully leased.
Property includes 22,100 SF building with 22' clear heights; second Bay Area IOS investment by JV partners.
Infill Newark location cited for East Bay transportation access; supply-constrained market drives acquisition thesis.
stories.summary: Sagard Real Estate and La Caisse jointly acquired a fully leased 2.84-acre industrial outdoor storage property at 6691 Clark Ave. in Newark (East Bay submarket). The site includes a 22,100-square-foot building with 22-foot clear heights suitable for contractor storage, equipment rental, and light distribution. This marks the JV's second East Bay IOS investment; emphasis on infill location and regional transportation connectivity in a supply-constrained market.
stories.impact: East Bay industrial/IOS supply tightness is pushing institutional capital into niche, high-barrier-to-entry segments (outdoor storage, contractor yards) with long-term, inflation-protected leases. For multifamily developers, this signals that competition for industrial-zoned infill land in the Bay Area remains intense; land banking for potential industrial or mixed-use conversion may face headwinds from competing IOS and logistics operators willing to pay strong per-acre prices.

stories.title: Standard Real Estate Investments, Endeavor Development Sell 174K-SF Industrial Facility in Minnesota
stories.excerpt: Standard Real Estate Investments and Endeavor Development announced the sale of Cobalt Business Center, a 174,288-square-foot industrial facility located in Mendota Heights, Minnesota. The project had strong leasing activity throughout construction and was fully pre-leased prior to construction completion. The property was subsequently acquired by a private investor. Located on a 10.1-acre infill site in Mendota Heights, Cobalt Business Center benefits from access to MSP International Airport and major transportation corridors. The surrounding area is home to major employers, including Amazon, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and Ecolab. Cobalt Business Center features 32’ clear heights; 15 dock positions, and 4,000 amps of power. “Cobalt Business Center is a great example of what happens when the right partner, the right product and the right market come together,” said Lindsay Louie, principal at Standard Real Estate Investments. “We believed in the Minneapolis industrial market, where demand for modern, well-located space has outpaced new supply, and the results proved that out.” The post Standard Real Estate Investments, Endeavor Development Sell 174K-SF Industrial Facility in Minnesota appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Standard Real Estate/Endeavor Development sold 174K SF industrial facility (Cobalt Business Center) in Mendota Heights, Minneapolis.
Property fully pre-leased before completion; strong construction-phase demand; located near Amazon, Blue Cross, Ecolab campuses.
Strong Minneapolis industrial fundamentals: modern, well-located supply outpaced by demand; sold to private investor.
stories.summary: Standard Real Estate Investments and Endeavor Development closed the sale of Cobalt Business Center, a 174,288-square-foot industrial facility in Mendota Heights (Minneapolis submarket), on a 10.1-acre infill site. The property was fully pre-leased prior to construction completion and sold to a private investor. The site benefits from proximity to MSP International Airport, major transportation corridors, and anchor employers including Amazon, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and Ecolab.
stories.impact: Minneapolis industrial market demonstrates tight supply-demand fundamentals and strong tenant credit quality anchored by major corporate tenants. For multifamily developers, this underscores the risk that land availability in competitive infill submarkets (especially near major employer clusters) is being captured by industrial/logistics operators ahead of residential. Consider early-stage land acquisition strategies near MSP Airport and northern suburbs before supply constraints push land prices beyond residential feasibility.

stories.title: Leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue Sells to Namdar Realty Group for $62M
stories.excerpt: Igal Namdar’s Namdar Realty Group has purchased the leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue for $62 million. The deal covers the entirety of the 11-story building at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 15th Street. Its Class B office and retail spaces sit at the intersection of Manhattan’s Flatiron and Union Square submarkets. The seller, a joint venture between Madison Capital and Lubert-Adler Partners, began marketing its leasehold interest in the property in 2021. Market sources at the time told Commercial Observer that the sale could net as much as $150 million. The ultimately $62 million transaction with Namdar Realty was finalized on Oct. 22, according to Traded, which first noted the sale. Meridian Capital Group’s Helen Hwang, David Schechtman, Brian Szczapa and Ian Shoenfeld facilitated the transaction. Namdar has roughly 90 years remaining on the leasehold term, according to Szczapa. Family firm Samco Properties and the family of Mark Lapidus, former global real estate chief of coworking firm WeWork, own the land underneath the property. The leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue was last acquired in 2016 by Madison Capital. The Midtown-based investment firm agreed to pay nearly $85 million upfront for the fully leased building, as well as $3.5 million in annual rent, according to The Real Deal. It is unclear when Lubert-Adler entered the arrangement. Currently, the building’s website advertises one full-floor availability spanning 15,227 square feet. Tenants there include WeWork, Dutch payment company Adyen and artificial intelligence video-editing startup Captions. An unnamed AI company recently secured a roughly 30,000-square-foot off-market lease in the building, sources fielding such hush-hush deals told CO earlier this month. The property’s ground-floor retail space is partially occupied by City National Bank, and another unit remains vacant. Representatives of Namdar Realty Group, Madison Capital and Lubert-Adler Partners did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Da
bullets: Namdar Realty Group purchases leasehold at 71 Fifth Avenue (Manhattan) for $62M, down sharply from $150M marketing estimate.
11-story Class B office/retail at Flatiron–Union Square intersection; ~90 years remaining on leasehold; marketed since 2021.
Deal signals distress in Manhattan office: initial ask-versus-achieved gap reflects persistent cap-rate compression and tenant flight risk.
stories.summary: Igal Namdar's Namdar Realty Group acquired the leasehold interest in 71 Fifth Avenue for $62 million, substantially below the $150 million originally projected when marketed in 2021. The 11-story building occupies the Flatiron–Union Square intersection with Class B office and retail tenants. The leasehold has approximately 90 years remaining; Meridian Capital Group brokered the transaction.
stories.impact: This reflects severe distress in Manhattan office markets and protracted holding periods for Class B assets in prime submarkets. The $88M write-down over five years signals that office-to-residential conversion or mixed-use repositioning remains economically challenging even in high-demand submarkets. For multifamily developers, the takeaway: office conversion projects in Manhattan face extended lease-up timelines and depressed underwriting; acquisition costs remain elevated relative to direct apartment development on multifamily-zoned sites.

stories.title: Podcast: How Yardi Is Becoming a System of Intelligence, with CEO Rob Teel
stories.excerpt: Rob Teel is the CEO of Yardi, the property management and real estate investment software company founded in 1984 whose platform serves owners and operators of commercial and residential space worldwide. He joined Yardi in 2003 and spent more than two decades leading its Global Solutions business, overseeing product direction, services, and client relationships across investment management, international, and commercial property owners before being appointed CEO in January 2026. Before Yardi, he was a consulting manager at Accenture focused on ERP and business process outsourcing, where he managed multinational systems implementations for Fortune 100 organizations. Rob is based in Santa Barbara. bullets: Yardi CEO Rob Teel discusses AI integration, SaaS evolution, and open versus closed tech ecosystems for CRE.
Focus on leasing chatbots, business intelligence platforms, and non-real-estate tech acquisitions (e.g., Sidero Labs).
Emphasis on AI as long-term competitive moat, not short-term revenue driver; private-company agility advantages over public peers.
stories.summary: Rob Teel, newly appointed CEO of Yardi (as of January 2026), discussed the company's transition toward becoming a 'system of intelligence' for property managers and investors. Topics covered include AI leasing chatbots, open versus closed AI ecosystems, build-versus-buy technology decisions, and acquisitions such as Sidero Labs. Teel emphasized Yardi's private-company advantage in pursuing long-term AI strategy without quarterly earnings pressure.
stories.impact: Little direct impact on near-term development underwriting, but signals that property management software vendors are racing to embed AI for operational efficiency (lease-up, tenant management). Multifamily developers should anticipate that operational KPIs (turnover, rent-up velocity, expenses) will be increasingly measurable and optimizable through integrated software stacks, raising the bar for asset quality and tenant experience expectations post-delivery.

stories.title: Children’s Rescue Fund Adds 9K SF at the Bronx’s 521 Bergen Avenue
stories.excerpt: Nonprofit housing and supportive family services provider Children’s Rescue Fund has upped its footprint at 521 Bergen Avenue. The charity’s executive offices expanded by 8,648 square feet on the South Bronx office property’s second floor in early October, according to an announcement by landlord brokerage JLL. The deal gives Children’s Rescue Fund a total footprint of 26,646 square feet and completes the lease-up of the redeveloped building, all six stories of which are entirely occupied by nonprofits. “Having a space that is accessible, flexible and well suited to our needs allows us to strengthen our operations and remain focused on delivering the critical services that families depend on,” Children’s Rescue Fund CEO Orlando Ivey said in a statement. The building owner is 521 Bergen Properties, and the building is managed by an affiliate of Rubenstein Partners. The landlord was represented by JLL’s William Korchak, Al Gutierrez, Edward DiTolla and Henry Warner in the expansion deal. It was not immediately clear whether the tenant worked with an outside brokerage. “Completing the lease-up of 521 Bergen Avenue is a significant milestone for the property and a testament to the vision behind its redevelopment,” Korchak said in a statement. Children’s Rescue Fund arrived at 521 Bergen Avenue in November 2025. Its initial lease spanned 18,000 square feet across the third and fourth floors, as well as a portion of the basement, Commercial Observer reported at the time. That deal carried a 10-year term with an asking rent of $39 per square foot, and the same terms applied to its recent expansion. The 55,000-square-foot building, located one block from the Third Avenue–149th Street subway station, also hosts child welfare organization JCCA and programming provider The Bridge. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Children's Rescue Fund expands by 8,648 SF at 521 Bergen Avenue, South Bronx; total footprint now 26,646 SF.
Expansion completes full lease-up of six-story nonprofit-occupied office building in early October; managed by Rubenstein Partners affiliate.
Nonprofit office absorption signals stable, patient tenant base in South Bronx emerging markets; supportive services co-location trend.
stories.summary: Nonprofit housing and family services provider Children's Rescue Fund expanded its office footprint by 8,648 square feet on the second floor of 521 Bergen Avenue in the South Bronx, bringing its total occupancy to 26,646 square feet. The expansion completed the lease-up of all six stories of the redeveloped building, which is now entirely occupied by nonprofits. Rubenstein Partners affiliate manages the asset; JLL brokered the transaction.
stories.impact: Nonprofit office clustering in South Bronx creates stable, long-term tenant base insulated from market cyclicality but indicates limited rent growth upside. For multifamily developers, co-location of social services and affordable housing in emerging South Bronx submarkets (e.g., near 521 Bergen) can enhance supportive housing rents and NOI through wraparound services; consider mixed-use deals that bundle nonprofit office with multifamily units.

stories.title: ANALYSIS: The Fed Holds Steady but the Cost of Capital Does Not
stories.excerpt: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rate steady Wednesday, pausing after September’s increase as policymakers weighed persistent inflation against the effects of higher borrowing costs. The decision has shifted attention to the timing of another potential hike and whether elevated Treasury yields will continue tightening financial conditions on their own. The Federal Open Market Committee maintained its target range at 3.75% to 4.00%, as expected. Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, preferring a quarter-percentage-point increase. The decision followed July’s hold, which drew three dissents favoring higher rates from Hammack, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan. Fed Upgrades Economic Assessment The committee acknowledged that inflation remains too high but said additional information would help it “determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the committee’s 2% goal.” Policymakers also strengthened their assessment of economic activity, describing growth as proceeding at a “strong pace,” compared with a “solid pace” in September. “While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient,” the committee said. “Productivity growth is strong, and capital investment is robust. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.” The decision leaves policymakers balancing economic resilience against price pressures that have shown signs of accelerating rather than converging toward their target. “Despite noise to the contrary, no change represents the most logical course of action at this juncture,” said Tom Briney, president and chief investment officer at Origin Credit Advisers. Maintaining rates, he said, allows earlier policy changes to work through the economy before officials make another move. December Hike Remains in Focus While the timing
bullets: Federal Reserve holds benchmark rate steady at 3.75%–4.00%; treasury yields rising independently tighten financial conditions.
Two dissents favoring rate hike; committee upgraded economic growth assessment to 'strong pace'; inflation still above 2% target.
Elevated uncertainty and geopolitical risk acknowledged; policymakers signal future hikes possible despite current pause.
stories.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee maintained its benchmark interest rate in the 3.75%–4.00% range on Wednesday, pausing after September's increase. Federal Reserve Governors Cook and Hammack dissented, preferring a quarter-point hike. The committee acknowledged persistent inflation above the 2% target but described economic activity as proceeding at a 'strong pace.' Treasury yields continue rising independently, tightening financial conditions without additional rate hikes.
stories.impact: Rising treasury yields and persistent financial tightening—even with the Fed on pause—will continue to compress cap rates and loan-to-value ratios for multifamily acquisitions and construction financing. Developers should expect higher construction loan costs (SOFR + wider spreads) and more aggressive lender underwriting on lease-up risk, vacancy, and rent-growth assumptions. The 'strong pace' growth language may defer rate cuts into 2025 or beyond, extending the elevated-rate environment longer than previously modeled.

stories.title: KKR Takes 49% Stake in Alexandria’s Campus Point Megacampus
stories.excerpt: KKR and Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc. announced on Wednesday a $475-million joint venture investment by capital accounts advised by KKR in Alexandria’s majority ownership interest in Campus Point by Alexandria Megacampus, a nearly two-million-square-foot life sciences campus in San Diego. KKR has acquired a 49% noncontrolling equity interest in Alexandria’s Campus Point investment entity, representing approximately 28.5% indirect ownership in the underlying JV. The investment provides Alexandria with flexible, long-term capital to support continued development, leasing and property enhancements. “Alexandria has built a premier Megacampus at Campus Point, supported by an exceptional tenant base and long-term contractual cash flows,” said Sam Caven, Co-Head of Acquisitions, Americas at KKR. “We are excited to collaborate with their team to support its continued development and drive long-term value.” Added Peter Moglia, CEO and CIO of Alexandria, “This transaction marks an important step in our efforts to optimize our capital structure and unlock value across our portfolio.” Eastdil Secured Savills acted as financial advisor and Proskauer served as legal advisor to Alexandria. Gibson Dunn served as legal advisor to KKR. The post KKR Takes 49% Stake in Alexandria’s Campus Point Megacampus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: KKR acquires 49% equity stake in Alexandria's Campus Point Megacampus (San Diego life sciences) for $475M.
Nearly 2M SF campus; KKR gains 28.5% indirect ownership; Alexandria retains control, secures flexible long-term capital.
Institutional co-investment signals strong life sciences fundamentals and capital efficiency in San Diego biotech/pharma submarkets.
stories.summary: KKR and Alexandria Real Estate Equities announced a $475 million joint venture investment in which KKR acquires a 49% noncontrolling equity interest in Alexandria's Campus Point Megacampus in San Diego. The nearly 2-million-square-foot life sciences campus includes an exceptional tenant base and long-term contractual cash flows. The transaction provides Alexandria with flexible capital to support continued development, leasing, and property enhancements while KKR gains approximately 28.5% indirect ownership.
stories.impact: Institutional capital redeployment into life sciences real estate signifies sustained demand for specialized lab/office space in tier-one biotech hubs (San Diego, Boston, Bay Area). For multifamily developers, this illustrates the risk that high-skilled labor concentration in life sciences clusters commands employer housing demand (workplace-proximate apartments, executive rentals); consider acquiring land near major life sciences campuses to serve the inflow of researchers, clinicians, and biotech workers, especially in San Diego's UTC and Torrey Pines submarkets.

stories.title: Blacksmith Software, Sona Technologies Lease 26K SF at Moinian’s 245 Fifth Avenue
stories.excerpt: The Moinian Group signed two new technology firms at one of its Midtown South buildings. Blacksmith Software, which provides support services to users of coding platform GitHub, leased 14,000 square feet, the entire seventh floor, of 245 Fifth Avenue, while AI-driven human resources firm Sona Technologies took all of the 12,000-square-foot 19th floor, according to the landlord. The Moinian Group did not immediately provide asking rents or the length of the leases, but the average asking rent in Midtown South was $71.43 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to a report from Lee & Associates. “245 Fifth Avenue continues to attract a diverse mix of businesses seeking high-quality office space in one of Manhattan’s most dynamic commercial neighborhoods,” Omar Sozkesen, vice president of commercial leasing for the Moinian Group, said in a statement. “These transactions reflect strong demand in the building and the strength of its location, flexible floor plates and distinctive character.” Newmark’s Scott Klau, Erik Harris and Ben Klau represented Moinian while AI-native brokerage firm Tandem Space negotiated on behalf of Blacksmith. Evan Kleinberg and Lenny Kohlmayer of Cornelia Street Partners negotiated on behalf of Sona Technologies. Tandem Space and Cornelia Street did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 245 Fifth Avenue sits at the corner of Fifth Avenue and East 28th Street, two blocks north of Madison Square Park. Other tenants in the building include WeWork, which signed a 55,000-square-foot lease in August 2025 — only its second lease deal since exiting Chapter 11 bankruptcy — as well as the Institute of Integrative Nutrition, which signed a 14,000-square-foot renewal in March 2025. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Blacksmith Software and Sona Technologies lease 26K SF combined at 245 Fifth Avenue (Midtown South), two separate floors.
Midtown South average asking rent Q3 2026: $71.43/SF; technology tenant concentration in Flatiron–Union Square district.
Moinian Group portfolio showing strong tech tenant demand; flexible floor plates and neighborhood character cited as draw.
stories.summary: The Moinian Group leased 26,000 square feet across two floors at 245 Fifth Avenue in Midtown South to technology tenants: Blacksmith Software (GitHub support services) took 14,000 SF on floor 7, and Sona Technologies (AI-driven HR platform) leased 12,000 SF on floor 19. Average asking rent in Midtown South was $71.43 per square foot in Q3 2026. Newmark brokered the transaction; Moinian highlighted the building's flexible floor plates and Flatiron–Union Square location.
stories.impact: Technology tenant migration into Midtown South (Flatiron–Union Square) signals stabilization and flight-to-quality in Manhattan office markets post-pandemic. However, tech sector layoffs and market volatility remain headwinds. For multifamily developers, tech worker concentration in Flatiron–Union Square (historically high-rent, young professional demographic) sustains rental demand but leaves multifamily exposure vulnerable to sector-specific downturns; diversified tenant employer bases remain preferable.

stories.title: Mattapan Site Will Contain 105 Affordable Housing Units
stories.excerpt: Colliers arranged the $8.75 million sale of 1590 Blue Hill Ave., a 1.63-acre site in Boston’s Mattapan neighborhood. A partnership between the Planning Office for Urban Affairs, a nonprofit housing developer affiliated with the Archdiocese of Boston, and JGE Development acquired the property from the McKeen family. The partnrship has secured city approvals for a six-story building with 105 affordable homes. The McKeen family operated a successful auto repair business at the site dating back to 1976.Colliers EVP Jeanne Pinado has advised the McKeen family over the past two and a half years since Colliers was engaged to market the property. Her experience developing multifamily properties in Boston was key to marketing the site to developers of affordable and mixed-income housing. “I am proud of my role in the eventual development of 105 affordable homes for Boston families by the Planning Office for Urban Affairs, which is serving as a catalyst for social justice through its work in housing development and neighborhood revitalization,” said Pinado. “This project will carry forward the McKeen family’s decades-long commitment to Mattapan.” The post Mattapan Site Will Contain 105 Affordable Housing Units appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Planning Office for Urban Affairs/JGE Development acquire 1.63-acre Mattapan site (Boston) for $8.75M; 105 affordable units approved.
Six-story building; site formerly McKeen family auto-repair business (1976–present); city approvals secured for affordable housing.
Nonprofit acquisition signals strong municipal incentives and community land trust momentum in Boston neighborhood revitalization corridors.
stories.summary: A partnership between the Planning Office for Urban Affairs (nonprofit housing developer affiliated with Archdiocese of Boston) and JGE Development acquired 1.63 acres at 1590 Blue Hill Ave. in Boston's Mattapan neighborhood for $8.75 million. The partnership has secured city approvals for a six-story building containing 105 affordable units. The site was previously operated as an auto-repair business by the McKeen family since 1976; Colliers facilitated the transaction.
stories.impact: Mattapan affordable housing pipeline and nonprofit developer momentum signal strengthening municipal policy support for workforce housing in historically underinvested Boston neighborhoods. For multifamily developers, this underscores regulatory shift toward inclusionary zoning and subsidy-dependent projects; market-rate rent growth in Mattapan remains constrained by competing affordable development and public land preferences. Consider market-rate development strategies in adjacent, less-targeted Dorchester and Roxbury submarkets with higher rent growth potential.
